2609.31054.title: Cheap, open agents make LLM pollution harder to mitigate
2609.31054.paper_summary: Large Language Model (LLM) pollution occurs when synthetic responses contaminate data intended to capture human behavior. High deployment costs have so far limited the risk posed by autonomous survey agents. However, open-weight models paired with open-source agentic frameworks may have removed this barrier. We compared the performance and detectability of nine agent configurations, ranging from fully open variants to closed commercial ones. Each agent autonomously completed a survey containing multiple response types yielding various detection checks. Fully open agents ran locally without usage fees and performed competitively with commercial alternatives. Open and commercial agents failed different sets of checks, and no single check reliably detected all agents, but open-text responses discriminated best between agents and humans. These findings identify fully open agents as a distinct risk for LLM pollution and support multilayered detection strategies emphasizing open-text analysis.
2609.31054.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLM）污染發生在合成回應污染了旨在捕捉人類行為的數據時。到目前為止，高昂的部署成本限制了自主調查代理所帶來的風險。然而，開放權重模型搭配開源代理框架可能已經消除了這一障礙。我們比較了九種代理配置的性能和可檢測性，這些配置從完全開放的變體到封閉的商業版本不等。每個代理自主完成了一項包含多種回應類型的調查，產生了各種檢測檢查。完全開放的代理在本地運行，無需使用費用，並且與商業替代品競爭力相當。開放和商業代理在不同的檢查集上失敗，沒有單一的檢查能可靠地檢測所有代理，但開放文本回應在代理和人類之間的區分效果最佳。這些發現將完全開放的代理識別為LLM污染的一個明顯風險，並支持強調開放文本分析的多層檢測策略。
